gaps.node_type: php_tag, text_interpolation, text, encapsed_string, heredoc, nowdoc
gaps.missing: HTML/text interpolation segments outside <?php blocks are not symbols; string interpolation internals are opaque
ini directives and shell hash-bang lines are not parsed as symbols or decision points

decisions.question: PHP property access `$this->balance`, `$obj->name`, `$this->svc->inner` parses as member_access_expression — when is it a READ (uses) vs a WRITE?
decisions.resolution: A member_access_expression that is the FIRST child of an assignment_expression is a WRITE (never a use). A member_call_expression / nullsafe_member_call_expression receiver is a call target, not a read. Everything else inside a method body emits uses -> the member name (isMemberRead). Node identity is compared by byte range because web-tree-sitter re-creates Node wrappers per call (=== never holds). Pure AST, never source-text scanning.

decisions.question: PHP global function calls flood the graph with stdlib edges — filter or keep?
decisions.resolution: PHP_BUILTINS (exported set, ~200 stdlib globals: string/array/type/math/fs/control/preg families) are filtered from call relationships. Method calls (member/scoped/nullsafe) are NEVER filtered — they are user code. The differential oracle imports the analyzer's EXACT set (single source of truth, no hand-duplicated copy).

decisions.question: Where do `use App\Models\User;` imports land — references or imports?
decisions.resolution: imports array ONLY (module = FQN, items = [alias or leaf]). The references relationship kind is reserved for require/include expression file paths (emitInclude). The differential oracle mirrors this split exactly.

decisions.question: Interface inheritance (`interface A extends B, C`) uses the same base_clause node as class extends — how are they distinguished?
decisions.resolution: By container node type: inside interface_declaration, base_clause children are ALL extends targets (interfaces inherit multiple parents); inside class_declaration, base_clause has exactly ONE child = the superclass (extends), and class_interface_clause children are implements. The dead literal 'interface_base_clause' (older grammar) was removed — probe-verified against the pinned wasm 2026-08-30.

decisions.node_type: method_signature / method_declaration / function_definition / def / sub (override resolution)
decisions.question: AnalyzeContext.overrideCompanion is never populated by production callers — what must analyzers that gate ALL override emission on it do for externally-declared bases?
decisions.resolution: M37.10 ruling (family-wide): the companion is optional enrichment, never a hard gate. Contract: in-file base declaring the method -> verified override (0.95 php/ruby/python/js/perl, 1.0 java/swift Pass-1); companion present -> companion-index resolution (0.85-0.9); otherwise deterministic Pass-3 first-parent guess at 0.5 with reasonCode 'first-parent-guess' and evidence tier 'inferred' — below the patterns.ts 0.7 threshold, counted as heuristic (honest suspicion) by the F5 differential. Gating on the companion alone silently dropped every cross-file override (php, ruby, python, javascript, perl); the inverse overclaim (swift guess at 1.0/structural) is equally a defect. Gated by F9-PROBE-M3710-* probes, per-language external-override fixtures + confidence pins, and 6 regression mutants.

decisions.question: M37.13 (php dual-lens #606): the extractive walk only recursed into node types it matched, and the call/creation processors (function_call / member_call / scoped_call / object_creation) lived ONLY inside walkBody (method/function bodies). Statements at program scope in PHP scripts, config/bootstrap files, and WP/plugin hook files ($x = new App(); $app->boot(); register_shutdown_function(...)) were silently dropped — the analyzer emitted ZERO edges for them while the differential oracle (a generic walk) derived all of them. Why was the corpus differential green despite this?
decisions.resolution: phpunit is class-heavy: only 4/300 sampled files (1.3%) carry top-level call statements, so the 60-file F5 sample rarely hit the shape — a coverage blind spot exactly like haskell HSD12/CSD1. Fix (M37.13): the main walk now dispatches function_call/member_call/nullsafe/scoped_call/object_creation wherever reached OUTSIDE a body, plus a generic child-recursion fallback for every unmatched node (mirroring the oracle's generic walk). Member READS are deliberately NOT dispatched there: the oracle derives uses for member_access only inside method/function bodies (inBody), which never reach the extractive walk (walkBody owns bodies) — verified parity on closures/arrows (anonymous_function/arrow_function are not body contexts in the oracle either). Pinned by fixtures/php/procedural-enum (global-sourced instantiates/calls equals pins) + mutant php/drop-top-level-procedural.

decisions.question: M37.13: PHP 8.1 enums implement interfaces via the same class_interface_clause shape as classes ('enum Status implements Labeled'), but the enum_declaration branch never read the clause, and the oracle mirrored the blind spot — enum implements edges were dropped by BOTH sides (a shared hole no differential can see).
decisions.resolution: Fix (M37.13): analyzer reads class_interface_clause on enum_declaration and emits implements edges (metadata isEnumImplements, tier structural) + implementedInterfaces payload; the oracle mirrors the same clause read so truth and analyzer stay in sync. Corpus-zero in phpunit (1 enum, 0 clauses in 300 files) so fixture + mutant gate it: fixtures/php/procedural-enum pins implements Status->Labeled/Tagged; mutant php/drop-enum-implements dies.

decisions.question: M37.13: the analyzer's processFunctionCall returns EARLY for the WordPress hook registrars add_action/add_filter (framework detection only, never a calls edge — they register callbacks, they don't call user code). The differential oracle imported the analyzer's PHP_BUILTINS but NOT this hook exclusion, so it fabricated calls:add_action/add_filter truth on every procedural WP-style file.
decisions.resolution: Ruling (M37.13): WP hook registration is framework ceremony — excluded from call edges on BOTH sides (single exclusion mirrored in derivePhpEdges, never a hand-duplicated copy). Add_action/add_filter still trigger WordPress framework detection. Pinned by fixtures/php/procedural-enum forbidRelationships (calls->add_action/add_filter) + mutant php/emit-wp-hook-calls.

decisions.node_type: method_declaration inside anonymous_class at top level
decisions.question: M37.13: 'new class { public function handle() {...} }' at top level — once the generic fallback descends into anonymous_class, its method_declaration nodes reached the extractive walk with owner=undefined and fabricated ownerless method symbols (a class-body member always carries its owner via pushMembers, so ownerless methods can ONLY come from anonymous classes).
decisions.resolution: Fix (M37.13): ownerless method_declaration = anonymous-class method — never symbolized (the class has no nameable symbol; mirrors walkBody's treatment of anon classes nested inside named methods), but the body IS walked so calls/creations inside are preserved (global-sourced). Pinned by fixtures/php/procedural-enum forbidSymbols handle + mutant php/symbolize-anon-class-methods.

decisions.question: M37.13: PHP 8.1 'new in initializers' (parameter default values, attribute arguments, static-variable and global-constant initializers) — these live in method/function SIGNATURES which the extractive walk continues past (bodies only). The generic walk would find the object_creation; the analyzer currently does not descend signatures.
decisions.resolution: Ruling (M37.13): documented boundary. Census on phpunit (300 files): 0 signature/attribute-context `new` occurrences (168 attribute_list nodes, none carrying object_creation). Corpus-zero shape; recorded here so the boundary is explicit rather than accidental. If a corpus ever exercises it, descend formal_parameters/attribute_list after walkBody with the same dispatch (no member reads possible there — signatures hold constant expressions).

decisions.node_type: base_clause / class_interface_clause with same-leaf fully-qualified base (namespace collision)
decisions.question: M37.13: a class may inherit from a DIFFERENT class that shares its leaf name in another namespace — phpmyadmin Setup\FeaturesForm extends User\FeaturesForm, phpunit interface Exception extends \PHPUnit\Exception, class InvalidArgumentException extends \InvalidArgumentException (the SPL builtin). Everything was leaf-collapsed, so the subclass's own name matched the base leaf: fabricated extends Self edges (12 in phpunit, 11 in phpmyadmin), VERIFIED @0.95 self-overrides (16 phpmyadmin, 2 phpunit — the in-file/companion override check matched the class's OWN methods), and `new parent()` -> self. Why did the F5 differential stay green? Both the analyzer AND the oracle leaf-collapsed identically — extends truth fabricated on both sides colluded.
decisions.resolution: Fix (M37.13): heritage-target resolution (heritageTarget). A QUALIFIED base/interface whose leaf equals the declaring class's name keeps its qualification (leading backslash stripped): extends FeaturesForm -> Forms\User\FeaturesForm, and override resolution then runs against the external same-leaf base (M37.10 first-parent guess @0.5/inferred — never verified, never self). A qualified base that qualification CANNOT disambiguate — global single-segment like \InvalidArgumentException — is unresolvable in the leaf graph: NO extends edge and no baseByClass entry (self-loop is always fabrication; family 'wrong edge worse than no edge' precedent, same as unresolvable new parent()). Analyzer metadata.baseClass/extends/implements/enum-implements and oracle derivePhpEdges + deriveTreeEdges heritage all mirror the same helper. Corpus result: self-extends 12->0 (phpunit), 11->0 (phpmyadmin); self-overrides 16->0 / 2->0; differential parity held at 100%/0/0 on both corpora.

decisions.question: M37.13 follow-up wave-2 (#606 master-review): PHP 8 nullsafe member READS `$this->svc?->name` parse as nullsafe_member_access_expression with the SAME "name" field as member_access_expression (`$this->svc->name`), but the walkBody member-read branch only matched member_access_expression, so every nullsafe read silently dropped the trailing member uses edge. 20 occurrences across phpunit+phpmyadmin+slim (4,231 files). Differential-invisible: the oracle's derivePhpEdges member branch shared the same shallow type gate, so F5 parity held at 0 missing / 0 unexplained while both sides dropped the read.
decisions.resolution: Fix (wave-2 probe-verified 2026-09-07): walkBody member-read branch now matches member_access_expression OR nullsafe_member_access_expression; the read/write + call-receiver byte-range gate is unchanged, so nullsafe WRITES (`$this->feature?->name = $v`) and RMW (`$this->feature?->name .= '!'`) stay gated exactly like the plain form (LHS name never a read). The receiver member (`$this->svc` / `$this->feature`) emits its own uses in both forms (csharp/java/ruby family precedent: the container is fetched to dereference). Oracle mirror identical. Parity probe: read/chain/plain emit [name, svc]/[deep, inner, svc]; write/augwrite emit only [svc]. Pinned by fixtures/php/nullsafe-member-reads (expect describe->name / describe->nested / describe->feature uses; forbid rewrite->name / bump->name) + mutants php/drop-nullsafe-member-read-uses and php/emit-nullsafe-write-as-uses both CAUGHT (299/299).
